case_data.title: AIAAIC
case_data.provide-a-brief-description-of-the-proje:
The AIAAIC is an open, independent, grassroots public interest collection of incidents and ethical controversies caused by and associated with AI, algorithms, and automation.

Anyone can submit incidents and access its database.

A team of volunteer researchers and activists are collaboratively maintaining the repository and elaborating a human-centered AI harms taxonomy (<https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.01294>).
case_data.why-is-this-project-important-to-include:
Although very imperfect in the way it involves the public (the project is open and voluntary but lacks mechanisms to enhance public engagement and actively reach out to affected communities), the AIAAIC has been one of the pioneers when it comes to registering AI systems harms, its database has been used to seed all other influential projects in that direction, and remains the only open and independent incident repository.
It has been used and cited extensively in academic research, journalism and CSO advocacy.
Its harms taxonomy (of which I am a co-author, so I might be biased) has also been influential and was one of the first published taxonomy to focus on harms and not on risks.

In spite of its limits, it is a project of historical and thematic signifiance to the case book (and arguably, its limits are also interesting to evaluate: difficulty of maintaining an active community with a global scope, lack of resources despite relative influence...).
project-goals: Quantitative: Generate statistical evidence on public attitudes to AI
Qualitative: Capture qualitative evidence on public attitudes to AI
Empowerment: Build community power with respect to AI
Audit: Review design or implementation of AI tools
